tech.title: Innovative Water Treatment for a Sustainable Future
tech.highlight1: Our IDR plant, a European pioneer in biological wastewater treatment, is equipped with state-of-the-art technology to ensure maximum efficiency and quality in processing wastewater from the leather industry in Igualada.
tech.text1: Operated by a team of highly specialized professionals in industrial water treatment, the facility upholds strict quality control throughout every stage of the process and fully complies with current environmental regulations.
tech.highlight2: In addition to serving the leather sector, the plant also manages non-hazardous liquid waste for other industries, contributing to the reduction of environmental impact across Catalonia's industrial landscape.
tech.text2: This facility is a testament to our shared commitment to a cleaner, more sustainable future, prepared to meet the environmental challenges of today and tomorrow.

about.title: United for a Sustainable Leather Industry
about.text1: Igualadina de Depuració i Recuperació (IDR) is a corporate initiative led by Leather Cluster Barcelona (LCB), in collaboration with tanners from the Rec district of Igualada. It was founded with a clear mission: to treat wastewater from the leather sector and ensure a cleaner, more environmentally respectful water cycle.
about.text2: Thanks to this alliance, IDR has become a unique platform in Catalonia, driven by a shared commitment: to promote a more sustainable leather industry.

partners.title: Partners
partners.subtitle: Our founding partners include leading companies from the leather industry, along with the City Council of Igualada and representatives from the textile and chemical sectors—all united by a strong commitment to environmental sustainability.

services.title: Liquid Waste Management for a Cleaner Industry
services.text1: IDR is the only authorized treatment plant in Catalonia specializing in the processing of non-hazardous industrial liquid waste.
services.text2: We add value to Catalonia's industrial sector by offering specialized water purification services for external companies, using advanced technology and sustainable processes.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.subtitle: At IDR, we are dedicated to providing sustainable purification solutions, constantly innovating to embrace circular economy models and moving toward a more efficient and environmentally responsible industry.

water.title: Water Quality
water.text: We apply advanced treatment processes to ensure the highest quality of purified water, protecting the environment through efficient water management at every stage of purification.

sustainability.title: Environmental Sustainability
sustainability.text: We are committed to reducing the ecological impact of the leather sector by treating wastewater from the leather transformation process using biological methods, minimizing its environmental footprint.

circular.title: Circular Economy
circular.text: We promote the development of alternatives to reintegrate purified water into the production process, contributing to a more circular system and optimizing the use of water resources.

innovation.title: Innovative Solutions for Emerging Environmental Challenges
innovation.text: We lead R&D projects aimed at optimizing existing processes and implementing cutting-edge technologies that enable increasingly comprehensive and sustainable purification—moving toward a circular economy and zero-impact model.

plant.title: Advanced Technology in Service of Water
plant.highlight: Our plant, a European pioneer in biological wastewater treatment, processes wastewater from the leather sector in Igualada. Equipped with state-of-the-art technology and managed by Tradebe—an international leader in industrial waste treatment—it ensures an efficient process that meets the most demanding environmental standards.
plant.text1: With constant and rigorous monitoring, we analyze wastewater daily, allowing us to accurately understand its composition and make real-time improvements to reduce environmental impact.

process.title: Biological Purification: Water, Air, and Life in Harmony
process.highlight: Our purification process mimics nature's own cycles, using water, air, and microbial life.
process.text1: The wastewater is treated with oxygen to support the growth of specific bacteria that break down organic matter and transform pollutants through the natural nitrogen cycle. In the final stages, oxygen-free (anoxic) bacteria convert nitrates into nitrogen gas, returning clean water to the environment with minimal impact.
process.text2: This system offers a highly sustainable solution that reproduces nature's logic at every step.

facilities.title: A tour of the facilities and the treatment process
facilities.text1: Every day, specialized technicians from the treatment plant collect water samples from the 26 associated companies for analysis. The results obtained allow for precise understanding of the composition of each company's wastewater, enabling them to take the appropriate measures to minimize environmental impact.
facilities.text2: Once at the treatment plant, the water undergoes physical, chemical, and biological processes to remove solids, suspended matter, and dissolved substances such as organic material and nitrogen, as well as color. Finally, the treated water is returned clean to the environment, meeting all established environmental standards.

analysis.title: Water samples from the tanneries
analysis.text1: Each day, specialized technicians from the treatment plant collect water samples proportional to the volume discharged by the 26 companies. These samples are analyzed in a specialized laboratory located at the A3 Innovation Center of the University of Lleida, on the Igualada Campus.
analysis.text2: These analyses allow for precise knowledge of the composition of each company's wastewater and help detect any variation or anomaly. Thanks to this data, companies can adjust their processes to reduce environmental impact, while the treatment plant continuously adapts its treatment system to ensure optimal performance.
analysis.text3: This constant adaptation between the companies and the treatment plant improves process efficiency, reduces pollution, and ensures sustainable water management.

pretreatment.title: Coarse screening
pretreatment.text1: Water enters the treatment plant's intake wells via collectors: one for industrial water and one for municipal water. These two water lines remain separate until they reach the first biological reactor. In these intake wells, coarse solids are removed using a clamshell bucket and filtration screens.
pretreatment.text2: After the coarse solids are removed, the pumping well moves the water to the next phase, where medium-sized solids are extracted using two step screens. Finally, in the grease and sand traps, fats are removed by flotation, and sand is settled out by decantation.
pretreatment.text3: Each type of waste removed at this stage is collected in separate containers for proper management.

chemical.title: pH Adjustment and Desulfurization
chemical.text1: Water from the industrial line passes through a pH correction system to adjust it for the following stages of treatment. Part of the industrial water is directed straight to the first biological reactor, while the rest is treated in desulfurization tanks, where sulfides are transformed into sulfates through the addition of liquid oxygen. Once desulfurized, the water flows into the first biological reactor.
chemical.text2: In addition to water treatment, the plant also includes deodorization systems such as chemical scrubbers. Air extracted from the pumping wells, desulfurization basins, and selective storage tanks is chemically treated to ensure no harmful pollutants are released into the atmosphere.

biological1.title: Biological Reactor I
biological1.text1: Once physically and chemically pre-treated, both industrial and municipal water enters Biological Reactor I. This tank is aerated using diffusers, and it fosters the growth of bacteria and protozoa essential for the degradation of organic matter.
biological1.text2: From here, the water flows through two secondary clarifiers where the sludge settles by gravity. The clarified water is transferred to a feed tank for Biological Reactor II, while the settled sludge is either sent for sludge treatment or recirculated to maintain the appropriate biomass volume in the reactor.

biological2.title: Biological Reactor II
biological2.text1: The plant includes four SBR (Sequential Batch Reactor) tanks, which are configurable to perform both nitrification and denitrification processes. Typically, two reactors are used for each process. These reactors are unique in their ability to carry out all phases of biological treatment within a single tank: filling, reaction, settling, decanting, and sludge purging.
biological2.text2: The water enters the nitrification reactors, where specialized bacteria convert ammonium into nitrates through aeration. The resulting clarified water is then directed to Biological Reactor III.

biological3.title: Biological Reactor III
biological3.text1: In denitrifying reactors, bacteria transform nitrates to nitrogen gas, which is released to the atmosphere, by adding new organic matter (desulfurized water) and in the absence of air. At the same time, tertiary treatment for color reduction is carried out using a coagulant.
biological3.text2: Sludge from all biological reactors is collected in a biological sludge sump, from where it is pumped to sludge treatment.
biological3.text3: Finally, the resulting clarified water reaches the outlet sump and is discharged to the municipal collector, which subsequently reaches the Vilanova del Camí municipal treatment plant.

tertiary.title: DAF (Dissolved Air Flotation)
tertiary.text1: The water from Biological Reactor III will be treated through a flotation system to enhance quality before being discharged into the municipal collector.

sludge1.title: Stabilization and Dehydration of Sludge
sludge1.text1: Sludge stabilization is carried out by adding lime slurry in the sludge chamber. Once stabilized, the sludge enters centrifuges for dehydration. A polyelectrolyte is also added to the centrifuge to flocculate the sludge and extract as much water as possible. The clarified water produced during this process is returned to Biological Reactor I.
sludge1.text2: Using an Archimedes screw, the dehydrated sludge is transported to storage silos, from where it is sent to the Jorba Composting Plant for bio-stabilization.
sludge1.text3: Deodorization systems are also in place here, using biological scrubbers. Air extracted from the sludge treatment room is biologically treated to prevent the release of harmful pollutants into the atmosphere.

sludge2.title: Sludge Bio-stabilization
sludge2.text1: Bio-stabilization of sludge takes place at the Jorba Composting Plant. The sludge delivered to the plant is unloaded and mixed with shredded wood to facilitate the bio-stabilization process. This mixture is moved into a decomposition area called the "meseta," where decomposition begins.
sludge2.text2: Subsequently, the entire meseta is turned over to aerate the material and promote further decomposition. When the temperature reaches 70 °C, hygienization occurs.
sludge2.text3: Finally, during the turning and screening phase, the grey compost is separated from the wood using a trommel screen. The wood is recirculated in the system, while the grey compost is properly managed.

quality.title: Management and Maintenance Facilities
quality.text1: The facilities include a laboratory where daily analytical controls are carried out to ensure the efficiency of the treatment plant and to analyze the liquid waste received. From the offices, the plant is managed and monitored, ensuring coordinated operation and overall control.
quality.text2: The plant has two blower rooms to supply air to the reactors and tanks that require it. Nebulizers are also installed at strategic points throughout the plant to prevent the spread of unpleasant odors near the facility.
quality.text3: Additionally, there are three tanks dedicated to the selective and temporary storage of liquid waste, allowing for differentiated treatment based on the specific characteristics of each type.

projects.title: R&D Projects for New Environmental Challenges
projects.highlight: With the mission of leading the transition towards a cleaner and more sustainable water cycle, IDR is fully committed to researching and developing innovative water treatment solutions.
projects.text: We collaborate with tanning companies, innovation centers, and other stakeholders in the sector to optimize wastewater treatment and advance circular water economy models that enable resource reuse within the leather industry—thereby reducing the consumption of natural resources.

innovation.title: Technologies for Advancing Towards Zero Impact
innovation.highlight: Through research into advanced technologies such as nanofiltration and reverse osmosis, we aim to achieve increasingly complete and efficient purification, oriented toward a model of minimal environmental impact and progressing toward zero impact.
innovation.text1: These systems remove contaminants such as salts, heavy metals, and organic compounds, improving efficiency while reducing energy and chemical consumption. This enables more sustainable water management aligned with global environmental goals.

quote.text: IDR, a pioneer in biological water treatment, drives sustainability and continuous innovation in wastewater management for the leather industry.

testbed.title: IDR Test Bed
testbed.highlight: IDR Test bed is a testing facility open to companies to test, develop and optimize advanced wastewater treatment technologies through membrane filtration systems.
testbed.text: With the willingness to share knowledge and facilitate innovation in the sector, IDR makes its testing facility available to other companies for advanced tertiary treatment.

hero.title: Commitment to the Environment and to People
hero.subtitle: Leading the transition towards a cleaner and more sustainable industry.

mission.title: The Path Towards a Zero-Impact Industry
mission.highlight: As a key part of Leather Cluster Barcelona, IDR has led the transformation of the leather sector toward a more sustainable industry.
mission.text: The wastewater treatment plant in Igualada, which currently treats the wastewater from 26 companies, is a pioneering model in Europe. Its advanced biological system significantly reduces both water consumption and the pollutant load associated with leather processing.

impact.title: Our results from the beginning to the present
impact.highlight: Thanks to this partnership, water consumption per unit produced has been reduced by 50%, and the pollutant load has also been cut by 50% over the past 20 years.
impact.text1: This collaborative model has enabled IDR's partner companies to become greener and more competitive, setting a new standard of excellence in the tanning industry.
impact.text2: Looking ahead, we continue to innovate and explore circular economy models to move towards an increasingly efficient and environmentally responsible industry.

quote.text: IDR enables wastewater from leather industry companies to contribute to sustainability efforts, driving a more environmentally responsible industry.

lifecycle.title: The Sustainable Life Cycle of Leather

circular.title: Commitment to the Circular Economy
circular.text: At IDR, we are committed to the circular economy as the foundation for sustainable development. Tanners recover hides—byproducts of meat consumption, the main protein source for over 90% of the global population—and recycle them to prevent waste. These hides are transformed into elegant, noble, and useful products for society, contributing to sustainability through their durability and by being both biodegradable and compostable.

byproducts.title: Byproduct Valorization
byproducts.text: For centuries, tanners have recovered this byproduct of the food industry and recycled it into high-value sustainable consumer goods. This practice not only reduces waste but also promotes responsible use of resources.

zero.title: Path Towards Zero Waste
zero.text: Catalan tanners, members of Leather Cluster Barcelona, remain committed to the zero-waste model. The cluster drives several initiatives to optimize the valorization of byproducts and reduce waste generated throughout the entire production process within the leather industry's value chain.

commitment.title: The Treatment Plant's Sustainable Commitment
commitment.text: At IDR, our commitment to sustainability is reflected not only in our water treatment technology but also in the internal practices we adopt to minimize our environmental impact and ensure a safe and responsible working environment.

renewable.title: Renewable Energy
renewable.text: 100% of the energy we consume comes from renewable sources, and we operate our own solar panel system to enhance energy efficiency.

chemicals.title: Reduction in Chemical Use
chemicals.text: Our biological treatment process optimizes the use of microorganisms to replace chemical agents, with the goal of minimizing environmental impact and promoting more sustainable and eco-friendly solutions.

audits.title: Environmental Audits
audits.text: We conduct regular environmental audits and maintain certifications to ensure our practices meet the highest standards of sustainability and environmental responsibility.

safety.title: Occupational Safety and Risk Prevention
safety.text: We take worker safety very seriously, with strict protocols in place to guarantee a safe working environment and full compliance with all health and safety regulations.

certifications.title: Environmental Certifications and Audits
certifications.highlight: At IDR, in collaboration with Tradebe, we manage the treatment plant according to the highest environmental standards, with a clear focus on sustainability.
certifications.text: Our audits and certifications demonstrate our dedication to upholding best practices in sustainability, innovation, and safety across all our services.

energy.title: 100% sustainable energy use certificate
energy.text: At our treatment plant, we are committed to sustainability and respect for the environment. Thus, all our energy comes from 100% renewable sources. The CNMC officially certifies that we use exclusively clean energy, reflecting our commitment to reducing environmental impact.

services.title: Non-Hazardous Liquid Waste Management Services
services.highlight: IDR offers treatment and management services for non-hazardous liquid waste, helping companies reduce their environmental impact.
services.text: Our philosophy of continuous improvement drives us to optimize treatment processes through customized physicochemical and biological treatment tailored to each type of waste.

licenses.title: Environmentally Guaranteed Liquid Waste Management
licenses.highlight: IDR holds an Integrated Environmental License for the management of non-hazardous liquid waste, with Manager Code: E-1706.17.
licenses.text1:
We are pioneers in Catalonia for combining two core activities:

·       Industrial and urban wastewater treatment

·       Non-hazardous liquid waste management
licenses.text2: Thanks to our advanced treatment technology, IDR can handle a wide variety of non-hazardous liquid waste streams with full environmental assurance.

hero.title: United for a Sustainable Leather Industry

who.title: The Tanners' Treatment Plant
who.highlight: Igualadina de Depuració i Recuperació (IDR) was founded as a corporate initiative of the Leather Cluster Barcelona (LCB), in collaboration with tanners from the Rec district of Igualada. The treatment plant is managed by companies from the leather industry itself, with the aim of ensuring a sustainable future for the sector.
who.text1: Our organizational structure is based on the active collaboration of our members through committees and working groups advising on traceability, technical development, and environmental impact. This ensures that every decision contributes to a more sustainable production cycle.
who.text2: Thanks to this alliance, IDR has become a unique platform in Catalonia, dedicated both to treating wastewater from leather tanning processes and managing liquid industrial waste from other sectors.
who.text3: After twenty years in operation, IDR has become one of the pioneering plants in Europe for industrial wastewater treatment and is now a reference point in the water industry. Over the years, it has treated wastewater from the tanning companies of Igualada affiliated with LCB, alongside other industries, and has been visited by sustainability professionals from over 30 different countries.

mission.title: The Sustainable Revolution of the Leather Sector
mission.text1: As part of Leather Cluster Barcelona, IDR has continuously improved processes in the leather sector through an innovative biological treatment system that has significantly reduced the industry's environmental impact.
mission.text3: This collective effort drives a forward-thinking leather industry, firmly committed to efficiency and environmental responsibility, bringing value both to the production chain and the local community.

vision.text: We aim to become an international benchmark in advanced industrial water treatment systems, leading the leather sector's transition toward a zero-impact circular water economy.

collaborators.title: Who We Work With
collaborators.text:
Collaborative Network
IDR is part of a collaborative network involving universities, associations, municipalities, and specialized companies. Together, we carry out R&D projects and promote sustainability within the leather industry.

tradebe.title: Tradebe
tradebe.text: A pioneering waste management company, Tradebe specializes in converting waste into valuable resources through innovative solutions, contributing to a greener and more sustainable future.

cluster.title: Leather Cluster Barcelona
cluster.text: A platform for cooperative competitiveness that promotes strategic and transformative projects to boost the Catalan leather sector's ecosystem, aligned with sustainability, circular economy, sustainable fashion, and shared value.

a3.title: A3 Leather Innovation Center
a3.text: Focused on research and innovation with new technologies for the leather sector, it develops projects aimed at producing premium eco-leather and improving the sustainability of tanning processes.

partners.title: Members
partners.text: Our founding members include leading companies from the leather sector, the Igualada City Council, and representatives from the textile and chemical industries, all committed to environmental sustainability.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: At IDR, we take privacy seriously. This privacy policy explains how we manage information on our website and online services. We are committed to protecting your privacy and being transparent about our practices.

section1.title: Section 01
section1.subtitle: We do not collect personal data
section1.text: We do not collect, store, or process any type of personal data from users who visit our website. This includes, but is not limited to, information such as names, addresses, emails, IP addresses, or any other data that could identify you.

section2.title: Section 02
section2.subtitle: We do not share data with third parties
section2.text: Since we do not collect any personal data, we do not share any information with third parties, whether companies, organizations, or individuals. Your interaction with our website is completely private.

section3.title: Section 03
section3.subtitle: Cookies and tracking technologies
section3.text: Our website does not use cookies or any other tracking technology to monitor user activity. We do not use analytics tools, advertising, or other forms of tracking.

section4.title: Section 04
section4.subtitle: Links to third-party sites
section4.text: Our website may contain links to other websites that are not operated by us. We have no control over the privacy policies of those sites and recommend that you review their policies before providing any information.

section5.title: Section 05
section5.subtitle: Changes to this policy
section5.text: This privacy policy may evolve over time. When we update it, we will revise the 'Effective date' and publish the new policy. To stay informed about our privacy practices, we recommend reviewing this policy regularly while using our services.

section6.title: Section 06
section6.subtitle: How to contact us
section6.text: If you have any questions about this privacy policy, you can contact us at info@idr.cat.
